claim: Recent deep mutational scanning study showed that allosteric hotspots in the tetracycline repressor (TetR) and its homologous transcriptional factors are broadly distributed rather than spanning well-defined structural pathways.
source: Recent deep mutational scanning study showed that allosteric hotspots in the tetracycline repressor (TetR) and its homologous transcriptional factors are broadly distributed rather than spanning well-defined structural pathways as often assumed.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous DMS studies on TetR family transcription factors.

claim: Hotspot mutation-induced allostery loss was rescued by distributed additional mutations in a degenerate fashion.
source: Moreover, hotspot mutation-induced allostery loss was rescued by distributed additional mutations in a degenerate fashion.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous experimental studies.

claim: The two-domain thermodynamic model accurately captures the in vivo activities of various TetR mutants with changes in physically transparent parameters.
source: The model accurately captures the in vivo activities of various mutants with changes in physically transparent parameters, allowing the data-based quantification of mutational effects using statistical inference.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing model fits to mutant induction curves.

claim: The two-domain model reveals the intrinsic connection of intra- and inter-domain properties for allosteric regulation.
source: Our analysis reveals the intrinsic connection of intra- and inter-domain properties for allosteric regulation and illustrate epistatic interactions that are consistent with structural features of the protein.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model analysis and experimental data.

claim: TetR can be generically divided into a ligand-binding domain (LBD) and a DNA-binding domain (DBD).
source: As shown in Figure 1A and B, TetR can be generically divided into a LBD and a DBD, disregarding its homodimeric nature (Leander et al., 2020; Takeuchi et al., 2019; Reichheld et al., 2009; Leander et al., 2022; Yuan et al., 2022; Scholz et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1 and citations to previous studies.

claim: Each domain of TetR features two conformations (relaxed/inactive and tense/active) that differ in free energies and binding affinities.
source: In the same vein of the classic allostery models (Monod et al., 1965; Koshland et al., 1966), each domain features two (the relaxed/inactive and tense/active) conformations that differ in free energies and binding affinities.
evidence: This is a model assumption based on classic allostery models.

claim: The two domains of TetR are allosterically coupled with a free energy penalty γ when both domains adopt active conformations simultaneously.
source: Importantly, the two domains are allosterically coupled, in that there is a free energy penalty γ when both domains adopt the active conformations simultaneously.
evidence: This is a key parameter of the thermodynamic model.

claim: The two-domain model accurately captures the induction data of 15 TetR mutants.
source: As shown in Figure 3A, the fitted curves accurately capture the induction data of all the mutants studied here, enabling the quantification of their biophysical parameters with little uncertainty (see Figure 3B and Table 2).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the fits shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The estimated binding affinities agree well with the range of reported experimental values.
source: these agree well with the range of reported experimental values (Scholz et al., 2000; Schubert et al., 2004; Kedracka-Krok and Wasylewski, 1999; Kamionka et al., 2004; Bolintineanu et al., 2014; Normanno et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with literature values.

claim: Epistasis is observed in all eight queried mutation combinations.
source: In the present analysis of TetR, epistasis is observed in all eight queried mutation combinations, which can be largely rationalized through physical reasoning.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental data with additive model predictions.

claim: The effect of a distant mutation like C203V on DBD energetics and inter-domain coupling tend to be dominated by mutations much closer to these regions.
source: For example, our results intuitively indicate that the effect of a distant mutation like C203V on DBD energetics and inter-domain coupling tend to be dominated by mutations much closer to these regions (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the epistasis analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Intra- and inter-domain properties are always modified together by mutations.
source: Although our model assumes no a priori correlation between the intra- and inter-domain properties of the TF, we find that they are always modified together by mutations (Figure 3 and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is observed in the parameter values of all mutants analyzed.

claim: The two-domain model is a more generic description of allostery compared with the MWC model.
source: We note, however, that the two-domain model is a more generic description of allostery compared with the MWC model.
evidence: This is argued based on the model structure and comparison with MWC.

claim: The MWC model contains at least four biophysical parameters when applied to two-domain systems.
source: Second, the MWC model, when applied to two-domain systems, contains at least four biophysical parameters (Daber et al., 2011; Chure et al., 2019), is thus more complex than our two-domain model, which requires only three.
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous MWC model applications.

claim: The two-domain model requires only three biophysical parameters.
source: Second, the MWC model, when applied to two-domain systems, contains at least four biophysical parameters (Daber et al., 2011; Chure et al., 2019), is thus more complex than our two-domain model, which requires only three.
evidence: This is a feature of the model as described.

claim: A comprehensive single-mutant TetR library was generated by replacing WT residues at positions 2-207 of TetR to all other 19 canonical amino acids (3914 total mutant sequences).
source: A comprehensive single-mutant TetR library was generated by replacing WT residues at positions 2–207 of TetR to all other 19 canonical amino acids (3914 total mutant sequences).
evidence: This describes the experimental library construction.

claim: The MWC model is not consistent with the observation that effector-bound TetR crystal structures are closer to the DNA-bound form compared to the apo crystal structures.
source: However, as pointed out in several previous studies, the MWC model is not consistent with the observation that effector-bound TetR crystal structures are closer to the DNA-bound form compared to the apo crystal structures (Motlagh et al., 2014; Reichheld et al., 2009; Hilser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on structural observations cited from previous studies.

claim: The ensemble allosteric model (EAM) presents a more flexible and detailed domain-specific view of allostery.
source: The EAM on the other hand presents a more flexible and detailed domain-specific view of allostery, which can be applied to more complex allosteric systems (e.g. allostery with intrinsically disordered proteins) (Motlagh et al., 2014; Hilser et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on comparison with the EAM framework from previous studies.

claim: The homodimeric nature of TetR is ignored in the current two-domain model to minimize the number of parameters.
source: It's noted that the homodimeric nature of TetR is ignored in the current two-domain model to minimize the number of parameters, and additional experimental data could necessitate a more complex model for TetR allostery in the future (see Appendix 1 section 'The simplicity of the two-domain model' for more discussions).
evidence: This is a stated simplification of the model.

claim: C203V and Y132A could not rescue a range of dead mutations including R49A, D53V, G102D, N129D, and G196D.
source: These examples might also explain why C203V, although being able to enhance the induction of TetR, fails to rescue a range of dead mutations including R49A, D53V, G102D, N129D, and G196D (Leander et al., 2020).
evidence: This is based on previous experimental observations.

claim: The negative correlation between ε_L and γ potentially offers a functional advantage of preventing mutants from regions of low allosteric response.
source: This feature potentially offers a functional advantage of preventing mutants from regions of low allosteric response (corresponding to upper right and lower left of Figure 5), facilitating efficient adaptation to new effectors during evolution.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed correlation.
